# Contributing

Open an issue with a reproducible problem or submit a pull request against `main`.
Describe the resulting behavior, affected contracts and tests you ran. Contributions
can add services or reorganize implementation; the current folder layout is a guide,
not a requirement. No AI tools or separate mod workspace are needed.
Use the [feature implementation guide](ARCHITECTURE.md#finding-and-extending-a-feature)
to locate contracts, services and hook owners. The HUD service shows
how larger features keep registrations, behavior and hooks in named parts.

## Setup

On Windows, install the .NET 10 SDK and Visual Studio or Build Tools with the
.NET Framework 4.8.1 targeting pack. Full integration tests also need a local SHCDE
installation with BepInEx and Script Extender. Never commit these proprietary assemblies.

Set `SHCDE_GAME_DIR` to your installation directory before opening `APIShared.sln` or
running commands. `GameDir` is the equivalent MSBuild property.
`SHCDESE_EXTENDER_DIR` / `ExtenderDir` override the usual extender directory.
The build driver detects MSBuild using Visual Studio Installer; `SHCDE_MSBUILD` is
an optional override. Paths are not tied to the maintainer's machine.
After a successful build, the APIShared and publisher BAT drivers can reuse these
local machine paths from `.local/build-proof.json` when the environment is unset.
Explicit environment settings take precedence; missing or invalid references still
produce an error before compilation. Direct IDE/MSBuild commands require their own
environment or properties.

## Tests

GitHub Actions runs source validation and the game-independent Core.Tests suite
without a game installation or the maintainer's surrounding workspace. Core.Tests
uses the public SharpZipLib 1.4.2 package in that environment; local runs with a
configured installation keep using the installed Extender library. Release-helper
tests always cover APIShared's own publishing decisions with simulated GitHub;
additional surrounding workspace-driver tests run when those drivers are present.
Real game/Extender integration remains part of the local build driver.

Tests use MSTest and appear in Visual Studio Test Explorer. Run the same commands
from PowerShell. The core suite needs no game installation:

```powershell
dotnet test tests/Core.Tests/Core.Tests.csproj
dotnet test tests/Core.Tests/Core.Tests.csproj --filter FullyQualifiedName~JsonTests
```

With the installed dependencies configured:

```powershell
dotnet test tests/APISharedTests/APISharedTests.csproj
dotnet test tests/LobbyModSettingsPresetTests/LobbyModSettingsPresetTests.csproj
& './build.bat' /nopause /noinstall
```

The full driver validates runtime contracts and installed interop, runs all suites,
compiles public consumer examples and prepares the plugin package. Remove `/noinstall`
to install it after closing the game; elevation is only needed for protected directories.
TRX results from the driver are stored in `.local/test-results`.
Successful builds also write `.local/build-proof.json`: source/reference fingerprints,
the source commit and package hashes. `tools/BuildProof.ps1` validates this local evidence;
it does not attest provenance independently. Game-free build-evidence tests run with
`./tools/Validation/Test-BuildProof.ps1` and in CI.
Release checks accept a clean subsequent commit when every recorded build input
and package hash still matches. The recorded build commit is retained; changing
compiled sources, packaging inputs or delivered files still invalidates evidence.

Core tests compile the actual dependency-free implementations. UnitAccess doubles model
the external SDK boundary, not native layout. Runtime tests use the real installed
assemblies and isolated memory/backend fixtures. Preset tests compile the actual
settings implementation with UI/session doubles; they verify persistence and convergence,
not rendering in the game. Controller tests use a plain settings host to verify role
filtering, mission isolation, reentrant setters and snapshot ownership without a UI.
Process-wide fixtures run serially and restore mutated state.
Temporary preset and atomic-file directories are cleaned up after each test.

Savegame participation tests cover
the generic plugin exclusion contract independently of any consumer mod.

Pull-request CI runs core tests and source/metadata/XAML checks on a GitHub-hosted
Windows runner. It does not claim to run installed-game integration or gameplay tests.
For changes affecting gameplay, report the relevant game checks and any remaining gaps.

## Compatibility and releases

Keep required public contracts and serialized formats compatible unless a breaking
change is explicitly intended and documented. APIShared owns its sources independently;
consumer mods use the public DLL. References in consumer packages use `Private=false`.
Avoid tests that prescribe source wording, filenames or implementation order. Test
observable behavior; retain byte/layout expectations where they express a native contract.

SHCDE destroys startup plugin components. Persistent services need a static root or
long-lived publisher. Published hooks remain installed until process exit; settings
use logical activation. The runtime's dependency-free JSON parser avoids loading extra
serializer assemblies. See [native compatibility](docs/NATIVE_COMPATIBILITY.md) before
changing native behavior and the [API catalog](docs/API_CATALOG.md) for threading rules.

Releases are prepared from a reviewed, committed and pushed standalone checkout:
`release.bat` builds and creates a GitHub draft. Version bumps belong to release preparation,
not test iterations. The maintainer's mod workspace pins a reviewed commit using a Git submodule;
contributors work in this repository with ordinary branches and pull requests.

## Documentation with a change

Explain public contracts where they are declared: prerequisites, owner and ID rules,
thread, lifetime, ordering, replay, failure and cancellation behavior where applicable.
Explain the responsibility and persistent call path at complex implementation entries.
Useful comments describe decisions and constraints rather than repeating names.

Keep the catalog's source map, integration guide and affected examples consistent with
API changes. Link to existing explanations instead of duplicating every feature in
several documents. Additional feature documents are useful only when inline contracts
and these guides cannot adequately explain usage. Preserve the README as a short entry;
propose a README addition after a new feature is complete. These expectations apply
equally to human and AI-assisted contributions.

# APIShared contribution notes

This is a standalone community repository. See CONTRIBUTING.md for setup and tests,
ARCHITECTURE.md for responsibilities, and docs/API_CATALOG.md for existing features.

- Explain public contracts directly in code, including relevant prerequisites,
  ownership, IDs, thread, lifetime, ordering, replay, errors and cancellation.
- Explain complex implementation entries and persistent call paths; avoid comments
  that merely repeat symbol names. Keep mod-specific algorithms in consumer mods.
- Maintain the catalog, integration guide and affected examples with API changes.
  Prefer links and inline contracts over a separate document for every feature.
- Document every new feature in the appropriate existing guide or catalog section.
  Keep README.md a short entry point with links where useful; this documentation
  maintenance is authorized by the maintainer.
- Preserve user changes. Do not commit or publish unless requested. Changes to runtime
  behavior need appropriate tests; documentation changes must not conceal behavior fixes.

These notes add no prescribed folder layout or AI-specific workflow.

## Shared services and consumer compatibility

- Check the API catalog, integration guide and architecture before extending a
  service. Reuse suitable Script Extender events and APIShared capabilities or
  registration brokers. A shared interception site has one hook owner; consumers
  must not install competing hooks or compile APIShared implementation sources.
- Keep reusable services and cross-mod hook coordination here. Consumer settings,
  activation rules, localized text and command engines stay with consumers. The
  public assembly must work with arbitrary mod GUIDs and without the maintainer's
  mod pack, workspace source links or neighboring repositories.
- Prefer additive extensions and retain process-lifetime ownership, independent
  failures and the documented original behavior. Specify prerequisites, ordering,
  caller thread, lifetime, payloads, private State, cancellation and exception
  handling; update affected public documentation, examples and behavior tests.
- Before every code change, assess binary, source and behavioral compatibility.
  Breaking changes include removing or changing public types, signatures,
  namespaces, identities or interface requirements, as well as changing defaults,
  payload/ID meanings, ordering, thread, timing, availability, lifetime,
  cancellation, exceptions, side effects or persisted data contracts.
- If a planned change breaks an existing public contract or could make a foreign
  mod using it stop working as intended, ask the maintainer explicitly BEFORE
  implementing it and wait for the answer. Explain the affected API, old and new
  behavior, consumer impact and a compatible alternative where possible. Ask also
  when a material compatibility risk cannot be resolved; independent compatible
  work may continue. General permission to edit APIShared, a version bump or
  passing tests of the maintainer's own mods does not authorize a breaking change.
  Unknown external consumers are not evidence of compatibility. Without approval,
  retain the existing contract; do not silently break it or introduce an unsolicited
  parallel fallback. This rule applies independently of Steam publication.

## Hot paths and event design

- Optimize code invoked continuously by permanent hooks and frequent publishers.
  Check actual demand, logical activation and recursion before doing optional work.
  Dormant services must follow the complete original path with minimal overhead.
- Keep early-return paths free of closures, LINQ results, formatted strings,
  context objects, reflection queries, file/asset access and game lookups. Inspect
  generated IL: a compiler can hoist a closure allocation ahead of a C# guard.
- Use existing durable events/publishers instead of Update-style polling. Retain
  process-lifetime callbacks and change logical state rather than executable hooks.
- Publish ordered immutable registration snapshots; execute callbacks outside
  registry locks. Preserve Pre/Post pairing, owner-private State, failure isolation,
  recursion rules and documented thread semantics through every optimization.
- Cache demand only when every activation transition is owned and accounted for.
  Dynamic predicates without change notification must remain dynamically evaluated.
  Serialize rare writes; keep frequent reads cheap without introducing false zero.
- Preload resources and prepare reusable metadata outside hot paths. Cache live
  game objects only under an audited lifetime contract. Bound diagnostics and avoid
  repeated atomic writes after a one-time marker has already been recorded.
- Measure allocations and execution time separately after warm-up, using equivalent
  scenarios and compiled production paths. Add IL/allocation regressions for fast
  returns. Report runtime and fixture limitations; do not infer an FPS gain.
- Prefer clear internal changes with measured benefit over blanket inlining,
  removing synchronization or pooling. Public event args may be retained by callers;
  do not recycle them or weaken immutable results and callback rollback contracts.
- Apply these rules to new or changed paths. They do not authorize broad unrelated
  service rewrites or public contract changes; existing compatibility rules apply.

# Audio binary update contract

The audio implementation lives under src/Audio; this is a native-update checklist,
not a consumer setting. Native provenance and fixed catalog/field offsets remain
hash-bound; a matching prologue alone cannot authorize a new game binary.

Native SHA-256: FBCB93195FC7EFCA9BDAC5204852EFDD76F9818F59A6711750D77C9CEF2831E2.
Managed SHA-256: BC8B6A395F01D48557DB413600C8DD8D1FDFD3ABDF97BFBBB68A3C56B04FD789.
NativeX64 SHA-256: 0843DD4C381A3E77DD6D8B51D5CCF95465B3FB49BFDF2980F39A212D774AADB0.
NativeContract holds the exact executable-section patterns and prologue bytes.
Targets: spatial wrapper 0x2960, flagged wrapper 0x2990, emitter 0x1A41E0.
Resolve the reference RVA first; if its pattern no longer matches, attempt a unique
executable-section fallback even on a matching hash. Log the method and actual
RVA. A moved target cannot be accepted against the old catalog/global layout;
context stays inactive. This is deliberate because original caller return PCs,
current-unit global 0x9302C4, native slot/stride and record contracts have no
independent proven cross-version semantic fallback.

Wrappers displace 15 bytes (4+3+8); continuation moves R8D to R9D. Emitter
displaces 14 (4+3+4+3); continuation writes X. Only NativeX64 Absolute is allowed.
Validate actual backend Scheme, target, displacement, zero PointerSlot, hook entry,
FF25 absolute patch, padding, copied prologue and trampoline continuation before
and after publication. The rooted intermediary reserves 0x38 aligned Win64 stack
bytes and forwards the original return PC as argument five. Execute it on copied
full wrappers after every backend change. No published hook may be reverted.

Audit all 91 source calls, allowed dynamic effect selections, type and coordinate
origin, pre-emission state changes, incoming edges, pending copies, all six pools
and slot reuse. Negative markers encode source/effect only; unknown sources stay
Unknown. Check GameUnit game IDs (1-based), manager+0x65C+id*0x490,
public slot1 manager+0xAEC, type+0x8A, state+0x2BC and X/Y+0xC0/+0xC2.
Revalidate the exact real processTestMap IL and public playSound/playSFX members,
private effect/clip table reflection and Extender decoder/resource publishers.
Update evidence per source/type; do not promote all units from one hearing test.

Map clips invalidate at unload/load/save-load/start Pre and should register after
OnPostLoad Post. Extender intentionally suppresses unload during native startup.
Callbacks must isolate exceptions to avoid its fallback repeating Vanilla. Imported
clips are borrowed references, not retained integer IDs. Custom playback uses
public playSFX with force=false, retaining global gains and channel selection;
Vanilla-specific forced effect channels/variants/throttles stay in the effect path.

Recheck Script Extender and the canonical Fixes clone for entry overlap and managed
playSFX overrides. Current inspected SE 2.14.1 and Fixes 1.25.1 do not own these
three native entries. Run standalone validations, all suites and consumer checks,
then game acceptance for new clip audibility, inferred actions and map transitions.
Errors deactivate the affected optional context or map-clip capability while
Vanilla, generic sound events and independent API services remain available.
